text:
kev: Heads up — seeing a p95 decode bump on canary after the recent merge (fused-batching-v2 / PR#4821). Shortseq workload, decode_p95 jumped ~18% (48ms -> 57ms) in CI. Canary was auto-paused.

anna: Ugh. Can you paste the profiler output or a flamegraph? Is this KV-heavy or cold-start?

kev: Quick paste from the perf run:
```
Flame top frames (sampled):
  decode_loop -> fused_op_dispatch -> attn_kernel_v2 -> cuda_memcpy_async
Hot path breakdown:
  kv_cache_lookup: 30%
  attn_kernel_v2: 45%
  memcpy/copy: 20%
  other: 5%
Observations: spike correlated with short sequences (<=16) & small batch sizes.
```

raj: That looks like the kernel selector is choosing attn_kernel_v2 for shortseqs now. v2 has better throughput for long seqs but worse per-token latency when KV hits cause extra memcopies. Did the scheduler change threshold in the merge?

darya: PR notes mention "scheduler heuristics: prefer fused kernels for fused models" — might have accidentally preferred fused kernels regardless of seq length. Can we bisect the commit range?

ci-bot: Perf job: https://ci.internal/perf/3165432099 — regression flagged: decode_p95 on canary > baseline threshold.

kev: Did a local bisect quickly. Range: merge-base -> HEAD. Bisect points to commit abc123 (fused-op scheduler: prefer-fused flag + new batch scoring). Reverting that commit locally brings decode_p95 back to 49ms.

sylvia: Nice find. So it's not an attention kernel bug per-se, it's selector + fused op interactions causing extra memcpy prefetch (memory bank contention) on short sequences.

anna: Short-term fix: pin kernel selector to attn_v1 for seq_len < 16 or when kv_cache_hit_rate > 20%. Can somebody draft a hotfix?

kev: Drafted a tiny override in selector:
```cpp
// shortseq override to avoid v2's prefetch path
if (seq_len < 16 && model.supports_kernel("attn_v1")) {
  selected = "attn_v1";
} else {
  // existing scoring logic
}
```
Bench locally: shortseq decode_p95 -> 50ms, longseq unaffected.

darya: That sounds reasonable as a quick patch. We should also add a regression test covering seq_len=8..32 with high kv hit rates.

sylvia: Also add a scheduler metric that logs kernel_choice breakouts so we can see selector distribution in canary.

kev: I opened PR #4855 with the override + tests + perf job: https://git.internal/r/4855. Requesting urgent review.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused (reason: perf regression). Current canary pinned to commit def456.

raj: After the hotfix merges we should run the canary again and watch decode_p95 + memory-bandwidth counters. If stable, unpause. Also plan a follow-up to refine the scoring function instead of ad-hoc overrides.

anna: Agreed. Will coordinate QA. Thanks for the fast bisect, kev. :rocket:
